title: Navin Fluorine International Ltd-$ - 532504 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Navin Fluorine Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 34% YoY to INR938 crore with EBITDA margin of 34.2%; FY26 PAT more than doubled to INR664 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR938 crore (up 34% YoY), operating EBITDA INR321 crore (up 80%) and PAT INR213 crore (up 124%). For FY26, net operating revenue was INR3,314 crore (up 41%), operating EBITDA INR1,082 crore at 32.6% margin (up 992 bps) and PAT INR664 crore versus INR289 crore. Management attributed about 70% of the EBITDA margin gain to new capacity and volumes and 30% to pricing actions. Management stated that it is monitoring Middle East-related raw material and logistics risks but has not yet seen supply disruption or demand destruction.

financial_highlights.metric: Net debt to equity; ROE; ROCE (31 Mar 2026)

financial_highlights.value: INR8.6 per share (430% of INR2 face value)

segments.name: HPP (Hydrofluoro products)
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR393 crore, up 20% YoY on realisation and volume growth; AHF plant commissioned and commercial supplies started in the quarter. Management said HPP has moved to about INR400 crore per quarter from INR250-300 crore, with more India sales.

segments.name: Specialty Chemicals
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR360 crore, up 39% YoY, led by scale-up of existing and new molecules. Management said about 13 new molecules were added in FY26, three of them in Q4.

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR186 crore, up 61% YoY. FY26 CDMO revenue was INR541 crore; management said about 50-55 molecules are in the pipeline, roughly half late-stage commercial and half early-stage.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin: management aims for about 30%, plus or minus 1-2%, measured on a full-year basis.
Net working capital expected at 75-80 days of sales in future, versus earlier guidance of 90 days.
Employee cost growth modelled at 7.5-9% per year.
Agrochemicals: about 80% capacity utilisation visibility for FY27; CDMO FY27 target of USD100 million is being pursued.
Capacity utilisation expected to rise to 70-75% in FY27 from 50-60% in FY26.
Nectar (fluorochemical) plant expected to reach 75-80% utilisation by end FY28; FY27 about 75%.
Management expects FY27 growth to be double-digit for the business, but gave no specific number.
capex_capacity: HFC/R32 expansion of 15,000 MTPA is on track for commissioning in Q3 FY27; the company also refers to 32 MPP of HFC capacity coming on stream.
Dahej MPP debottlenecking capex targeted for commissioning in Q3 FY27.
Chemours project (initial capacity to accelerate market adoption) expected to complete by end June or early July 2026; future capex to be decided after about 18 months of market understanding.
cGMP4 (dedicated Fermion block) commissioned in Q4 FY26 (December per management); management said Phase 2 (cGMP5) is possible with space for 5-7 molecules.
AHF plant commissioned in February 2026; revenue expected to flow mainly from FY28.
demand_pricing: Management reports robust customer demand with no demand destruction seen so far; order visibility is solid, and restocking may follow once conditions improve.
Raw material inflation (sulfur, methanol) has been largely passed on to customers; management said there were no shutdowns due to raw material shortages.
Contracts differ: service-play contracts have pass-through mechanisms; product contracts are being renegotiated.
R32 pricing: management said China prices are near USD9/kg and that the USD600-875 range was a downside case used for investment approval.
Management said agrochemical pricing is subdued and expected to rise more slowly than volumes in FY27.
Middle East: export exposure is small; roughly INR15-16 crore of Middle East shipments were missed in Q4 and are excluded from Q1 numbers.
Management said the Chinese market could absorb Nectar product at reasonable margins.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin gain comes from currency versus operations, and how will raw material inflation be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said currency and inflation largely offset each other. Of the roughly 990 bps EBITDA margin gain, about 70% came from capacity and volume and about 30% from pricing. Pass-through clauses cover service contracts.

qa_highlights.question: Is the R32 pricing downside case of USD600-875 realistic given new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the USD600-875 range was a downside case that is always prepared for investment approval, and its belief is driven by demand-supply and GWP dynamics.

qa_highlights.question: Will HPP and Specialty Chemicals grow at high double digits in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a number but said it would be surprised if growth were not double-digit, citing utilisation going from 50-60% to 70-75%, the HF plant, Nectar, Chemours and cGMP4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Nectar plant's balance of volumes and how will the second 50% be placed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said qualifications are under way with 2-3 customers beyond the marquee customer. Utilisation is targeted at 75% in FY27 and the balance later, with some shipments already made outside contracted volumes.

qa_highlights.question: Why did contract liabilities rise to about INR211 crore from INR239 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said contract liabilities reflect customer capital contributions for the Chemours project and the marquee Nectar molecule project.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 HPP revenue decline sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a planned shutdown and a catalyst recharge at one plant ahead of the heat season, plus about INR15-16 crore of Middle East shipments that did not go out.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict: raw material (sulfur, methanol) availability, energy prices and logistics; management said there has been no disruption so far.
Government R32/HFC quota allocation and new capacity coming in CY26-27 could pressure R32 pricing; management disputed the downside case.
Pricing lag on calendar-year contracts for HFO and CDMO if raw material inflation persists.
Nectar merchant volumes depend on qualifications of 2-3 customers beyond the marquee customer; utilisation is slower than originally planned.
Chemours and Dahej commissioning timelines (end June / early July 2026 and Q3 FY27) and the R32 timeline in Q3 FY27.
Margin sustainability: management guides about 30% for FY27 with a plus or minus 1-2% range, against a 34.2% Q4 margin.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operations and FY27 visibility, but guarded on Middle East risk, R32 pricing and currency-driven margin benefits, which management largely declined to quantify.
key_quotes: So far, we have not seen any disruption. We have seen inflation go through.

I think it's about 990 basis points from FY to FY, you will see 70% of that for Navin is coming from our capacities coming on the ground, our volumes going up and 30% is coming from affirmative actions on pricing that we've taken.
So therefore, we are talking of the 75% this year and then the balance next year.
I would be surprised if it's not double-digit, but I'm happy to clarify if it is not separately.

adds.what: AHF plant (HPP), commissioned Feb 2026; revenue mainly from FY28

growth.why: Management expects double-digit FY27 business growth without a number, backed by utilisation rising to 70-75% from 50-60%, HFC/R32 15,000 MTPA expansion due Q3 FY27, Dahej debottlenecking, and ~80% agchem visibility, with CDMO FY27 $100m target reiterated and EBITDA margin guided ~30% ±1-2%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides FY27 EBITDA margin about 30% (plus or minus 1-2%) versus 32.6% for FY26 and 34.2% in Q4, and says agrochemical pricing will rise more slowly than volumes; about 30% of the 990 bps gain came from pricing and currency offset inflation.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q3 FY27 (HFC/R32 15,000 MTPA and Dahej MPP debottlenecking);
rows.why: HFC/R32 15,000 MTPA expansion is on track for Q3 FY27 commissioning, Dahej debottlenecking targeted Q3 FY27, and Chemours project expected to complete end June or early July 2026; AHF plant already commissioned in Feb 2026 with revenue mainly from FY28.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Utilisation expected to rise to 70-75% in FY27 from 50-60% in FY26, HFC/R32 15,000 MTPA due Q3 FY27, and agrochemicals about 80% capacity visibility; HPP has moved to about INR400 crore per quarter from INR250-300 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is about 80% today per management, but R32 quota uncertainty and the Chemours follow-on capex is to be decided after about 18 months of market understanding; cGMP5 Phase 2 is possible with space for 5-7 molecules.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Utilisation rising to 70-75% in FY27 from 50-60% in FY26, plus CDMO $100m FY27 target still held, could push growth above the double-digit guide, but management gave no number.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at about 30% (plus or minus 1-2%) versus a 34.2% Q4 margin, with Middle East raw material and logistics risk and R32 pricing pressure from new capacity; Middle East shipments of INR15-16 crore were missed in Q4.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: About 13 new molecules were added in FY26 (three in Q4), 50-55 CDMO molecules are in the pipeline with about half late-stage commercial, and Nectar qualifications are under way with 2-3 customers.

rows.label: Net working capital at 75-80 days vs 90 days earlier guidance
rows.why: Net working capital days fell to 74 from 90 and management now guides 75-80 days of sales, against prior indicative 90 days.

rows.label: Robust demand with no demand destruction; Middle East exposure small
rows.why: Management reports robust customer demand and solid order visibility, with Middle East export exposure small and only INR15-16 crore of Q4 shipments missed and excluded from Q1.

rows.label: R32 pricing pressure from new capacity and quota
rows.why: China R32 prices are near USD9/kg, management says USD600-875 range was a downside case, and a competitor R32 capacity above 120,000 MT by FY27 raises supply risk; quota allocation is the key question.

tone.note: Management was confident on utilisation, the Q3 FY27 capacity start-ups and the CDMO $100m target, but cautious on Middle East raw-material risk, R32 pricing and the currency-driven margin benefit it declined to quantify; analysts pressed on R32 quota and competitor capacity above 120,000 MT.
